body:
Saudi Venture Capital (SVC) invested in Jadwa Investment’s flagship private credit fund. Thus, backing a financing strategy that aims to expand Shariah-compliant funding options for businesses in Saudi Arabia and the wider region.

The fund has committed more than SAR 400 million across five investments to date. It also expects to complete a sixth investment during the fourth quarter of 2026.

The investment highlights the growing role of private credit in financing businesses that need alternatives to traditional lending and equity funding. By supporting Jadwa’s fund, SVC aims to broaden access to financing for Saudi small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), while strengthening the Kingdom’s private capital market.

For growing companies, private credit can provide more flexible financing structures tailored to their business needs. It also offers institutional and private wealth investors another avenue to participate in the region’s private capital market.

Jadwa Investment, investment management and advisory firm, manages the fund, which focuses on providing Shariah-compliant financing solutions to companies operating primarily in Saudi Arabia and across the wider region.

Established in 2018, SVC is a subsidiary of the SME Bank, which falls under Saudi Arabia’s National Development Fund. The company supports startup and SME financing from pre-seed through pre-IPO stages through investments in funds and direct investments in businesses.

Headquartered in Riyadh, Jadwa Investment manages more than SAR 110 billion in client assets across public equity, private equity, real estate, private credit, fixed income, and money market investments.

SVC’s investment brings a government-backed financing institution into Jadwa’s private credit strategy, connecting public sector support with private investment management. The partnership also adds momentum to Saudi Arabia’s efforts to diversify funding channels for SMEs beyond conventional financing and equity investment.

For Jadwa, the investment strengthens its flagship fund’s investor base and supports its position in the region’s private credit market.

The fund’s next milestone is its expected sixth investment in the final quarter of 2026. Its deployment pace and ability to attract further institutional capital will offer a clearer picture of how private credit is developing as a financing channel for Saudi businesses.
